G1_safe_deny_allow_tests.description: For each of three operation types (exec, file-open, network-connect), a single self-contained pod runs an internal test loop (not invoked via kubectl exec -- see exclusions.md for why) attempting a designated ALLOW target and a designated DENY target, n reps each. Every repetition is an independent syscall attempt against a live, enforce-mode RuntimeSecurityPolicy with the corresponding operation's DefaultAction=deny and exactly one explicit allow-list entry.

file.allow: /tmp/allowed-testfile (created by the pod's own process, matching the exact-match allow-list entry -- see exclusions.md on AllowedPathPrefixes' real semantics)

network.allow: 127.0.0.1:9999 (nothing listens; ECONNREFUSED at the TCP layer, not EPERM at the LSM layer, is the expected/correct allow-path outcome)

G1_safe_deny_allow_tests.reps_note: exec meets the protocol's explicit n>=30 target for the important microbenchmark exactly; file/network use n=15, a documented scope reduction under real time constraints, consistent with every prior experiment in this campaign.
recorded_fields: policy (RuntimeSecurityPolicy spec, captured in environment.json/raw ebpf map dump)

G2_repetitions.description: n=30 for exec (meets '>=30 per important allow/deny condition if practical' exactly), n=15 for file/network (documented reduction).

G3_critical_conclusion.verifier_level_claim: SUPPORTED: real BPF-LSM programs (lsm_exec, lsm_file_open, lsm_connect, lsm_bpf_lock) load and verify successfully on this worker node's live kernel, confirmed via agent logs (mode=enforce) and direct bpftool prog list/dump inspection (substantial, non-stub xlated bytecode for all 4 programs, correct map references).
G3_critical_conclusion.policy_propagation_claim: SUPPORTED: RuntimeSecurityPolicy.Spec.EnforcementMode/Exec.DefaultAction/AllowedPaths correctly reach the kernel's cgroup_configs and exec_rules eBPF maps, confirmed via direct bpftool map dump (not inferred from CRD state alone) -- ground truth in raw/ebpf-map-groundtruth.txt.
G3_critical_conclusion.allow_path_claim: SUPPORTED: designated ALLOW targets succeeded in 100% of reps (exec 30/30, file 15/15) under confirmed enforce-mode policy.
G3_critical_conclusion.pre_effect_denial_claim: NOT SUPPORTED BY THIS TESTING: designated DENY targets were not observed to return EPERM or be blocked pre-effect in ANY of the 60 deny-condition reps (exec 30, file 15, network 15), despite the kernel-side configuration being independently confirmed correct for denial. This is reported as an honest, unresolved negative finding, not fabricated or silently omitted -- see summary.md and exclusions.md for the full diagnostic trail and candidate hypotheses.
G3_critical_conclusion.scope_statement_per_master_prompt: Because the pre-effect denial claim is not supported, this experiment does NOT establish 'RuntimeGuard claims experimentally demonstrated CPU BPF-LSM pre-effect enforcement' in the protocol's own terms. It DOES establish that real (not audit-only) BPF-LSM programs load, verify, and correctly gate the ALLOW path on this hardware -- a necessary but, per this task's own explicit framing, not sufficient condition for that stronger claim.

task_12_followup_2026_08_14.trigger: User explicitly rejected the original G3 finding as a permanently unresolved mystery and required further investigation; Azure infrastructure was re-provisioned specifically to continue it.
task_12_followup_2026_08_14.new_instrumentation: COUNTER_LSM_HOOK_ENTERED (common.h/agent.bpf.c): a permanent, unconditional entry counter on every lsm/* program, bumped before any cfg lookup or decision logic -- distinguishes 'hook never invoked' from 'hook invoked but decision not enforced'.
task_12_followup_2026_08_14.finding_1_task11_interaction: With Task 11 worker-trust-validation active (the default), G1's hand-patched RuntimeSecurityPolicy is correctly rejected as tampering (hash(P_received) != hash(derive(D))), falling back to deny-all -- Task 11 working as designed, and a genuine new finding that G1's test methodology is incompatible with an active D->P trust boundary.
task_12_followup_2026_08_14.finding_2_original_mystery_did_not_repro: With worker-trust-validation temporarily disabled (--worker-trust-validation=false, reproducing Task 10's original pre-Task-11 conditions), the ORIGINAL finding (deny conditions silently falling through to allow) did NOT reproduce. Instead, a different failure mode occurred: exec/file ALLOW and DENY conditions were both denied (network unaffected).
task_12_followup_2026_08_14.finding_3_decisive_evidence_not_runtimeg: A temporary per-event debug log (since removed) proved zero EVENT_TYPE_EXEC ring-buffer events were emitted despite 30/30 EPERM results and despite COUNTER_LSM_HOOK_ENTERED confirming the hook fires -- proof (not inference) that lsm_exec's own decision logic and emit_event() calls were never reached, because its own `if (ret != 0) return ret;` guard (deliberate, correct fmod_ret-chain-respecting code) returned early due to a nonzero ret from an earlier LSM in the node's lsm= chain (lockdown, capability, landlock, yama -- all before bpf).
task_12_followup_2026_08_14.finding_4_apparmor_ruled_out: Direct A/B test (container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/g1-runner: unconfined) produced an identical result, ruling out AppArmor specifically.
task_12_followup_2026_08_14.finding_5_platform_reproducibility_gap: Two independent, nominally-identical Azure provisioning instances (same Terraform config, same VM SKU, same kernel 6.8.0-1064-azure, same GRUB lsm= list) exhibited DIFFERENT BPF-LSM enforcement behavior for the same test. This cross-provisioning non-reproducibility is itself a new, real, and reportable finding, external to RuntimeGuard's own implementation.
task_12_followup_2026_08_14.revised_pre_effect_denial_claim: STILL NOT SUPPORTED, now with direct (not inferential) evidence that RuntimeGuard's own code is not the acting cause in either observed failure pattern. Candidate root cause narrowed to interaction with an earlier-in-chain LSM (most likely landlock, not confirmed) intercepting bprm_check_security/file_open before RuntimeGuard's own bpf LSM hook runs its own logic. Root cause not fully identified; see exclusions.md's Task 12 follow-up section.
task_12_followup_2026_08_14.raw_data_caveat: A fixed (non-per-run-unique) output filename in this follow-up's own diagnostic script caused 3 of 4 reruns' full per-record raw JSON to be overwritten before archival; only aggregate per-op/per-condition counts survive for those runs (computed and recorded immediately after each run, before the next overwrote it). Disclosed in exclusions.md, not hidden. Does not affect the original Task 10 dataset (g1-results.json), which is untouched.
